sections.title: Your route from governance user to practitioner
sections.intro: A practical field guide for governance practitioners • Research checked 10 October 2026

blocks.text: Your strongest entry point is to use Databricks as a workbench for governance evidence: discover what is registered, inspect what the data actually contains, measure quality, connect technical fields to business meaning, and produce repeatable evidence for releases. Your Collibra experience gives you the business context. The new skills are writing transformations, understanding execution and permissions, and making checks reproducible.

This guide is written for an end user in a vendor-provisioned company sandbox. It does not assume that you administer the platform, own cloud infrastructure, or can enable every feature. AWS examples are used because you work with S3; your Databricks workspace cloud is not confirmed. Core SQL and governance ideas apply across clouds, while networking, identities, regions, and some capabilities differ.

blocks.text: What this guide covers

A broad map of the platform, deeper coverage of the capabilities relevant to governance, sixteen exercises, a reporting catalog, a department pilot, limitations, and a certification plan. This is a substantial foundation, not a claim to document every API or make someone an expert by reading alone. Expertise comes from repeated implementation, failure investigation, and review of production decisions.
What has and has not been verified

Product descriptions are grounded in the linked official Databricks and Collibra sources. The synthetic lab results are designed to be independently checkable. No company Databricks workspace was connected or inspected for this report; code has not been executed there. Feature availability, runtime behavior, policies, quotas, and permissions must be checked in your sandbox. Instructions labeled optional or platform-assisted are intentionally separate from the core SQL path.

P2P is interpreted here as promotion to production or a comparable governed release process. If your department uses a different expansion, apply the evidence and approval ideas to that process; this report does not redefine your company policy.

sections.title: 1. The mental model: five different layers

blocks.text: Imagine a loan-data workroom. S3 holds files. Tables give those files usable structure. Compute performs the work. Unity Catalog identifies and governs assets. The workspace is where people write, inspect, schedule, and present that work. Mixing these layers causes many beginner mistakes.

rows: Storage
The bytes: objects, files, and table data.
An S3 prefix may contain CSVs, JSON, documents, and older copies. A prefix is not automatically one business dataset.
Table format
Rules for storing and changing table data. Delta Lake adds transaction metadata to data files.
Updates, merges, and reproducible snapshots are easier to reason about than a folder of overwritten CSVs.
Compute
Resources that execute SQL, Python, and other supported workloads.
A SQL warehouse runs your report query. Notebook/job compute runs transformations. A notebook alone is not a running engine.
Governance
Names, ownership, privileges, policies, discovery, and captured lineage.
Unity Catalog controls supported access paths; it does not erase independent S3 IAM permissions.
Workspace
A collaboration and execution surface.
Notebooks, queries, dashboards, job definitions, Git folders, and settings live here. A workspace folder is not a database schema.

blocks.text: The namespace you will type constantly

A metastore contains governance metadata for catalogs and their objects. A catalog groups schemas; a schema groups tables, views, volumes, functions, and other supported objects. A table contains rows and columns. A volume provides governed file access. A view stores a query definition; it does not ordinarily store a separate result copy. A materialized view persists computed results and has refresh behavior.
What lakehouse means in practice

The useful idea is to combine flexible object storage with table management and analytical processing. It does not mean every S3 object has already been cataloged, every source system has moved, or every workload belongs in the same table engine. A source inventory can exist before data is ingested, and a catalog entry can exist without giving you permission to read the data.

blocks.title: Check your understanding
blocks.text: Can you answer each separately: Where are the bytes? What is the table name? What engine runs the query? Which identity runs it? Which policy permits it? Who defines its business meaning? These six questions are a better troubleshooting tool than remembering a product logo.

sections.title: 2. Databricks and Collibra: a deliberate division of work

blocks.text: Recommended operating model for your department: Collibra remains the approved enterprise record for stewardship, glossary decisions, initiatives, issues, and release approvals where those processes already live. Databricks supplies executable data checks, pipeline operation, access enforcement, and technical evidence. This is a design recommendation, not an automatic product boundary: both platforms have catalog and semantic capabilities.

blocks.text: Where current integration helps

Collibra documents an Edge-based Unity Catalog integration for inbound technical metadata and configured outbound attribute-to-tag synchronization. Profiling/sampling uses additional JDBC setup. Technical lineage has its own setup. Do not assume that enabling the catalog connector also enables profiling, lineage, and every outbound field. Confirm your installed Collibra and Edge versions and capability configuration with the integration owner.

Current Collibra documentation limits outbound synchronization to supported assets ingested through the Unity Catalog integration. Blank mapped tag values can remove destination tags; governed-tag values must match allowed values. Responsibilities and data-quality scores are among the outbound items the documentation says are not yet supported. Treat synchronization as a configured contract with reconciliation, not a universal two-way copy.
Business semantics now overlap

Current Databricks documentation includes metric views, business domains, Pages for business concepts, and certification/deprecation signals. You may also encounter newer Discover and Genie experiences. If enabled, use them to surface approved definitions and reusable metrics; do not let local copies silently diverge from your enterprise glossary. A certified label is a trust signal, not proof that every control was executed.

blocks.title: Practical first decision
blocks.text: Choose one small loan dataset. Agree who owns each metadata field, the identifier used to match assets, the direction of each synchronization, the refresh cadence, and what happens when a term or tag is removed. Write these choices before attempting broad synchronization.

sections.title: 5. Inventory, profiling, and identification are different jobs

rows: What exists?
S3 inventory, database inventories, registered catalog objects, and a defined coverage scope.
Calling the objects you can see a complete enterprise inventory.
What is its structure?
Schemas, types, nesting, file formats, and schema versions.
Treating a file extension as proof of consistent contents.
What values are present?
A profile with scan scope, sample method, timing, and distribution statistics.
Assuming a sample proves absence of sensitive or invalid values.
What does it mean?
Approved business definition, grain, domain, lineage, and steward validation.
Mapping a field named id to a business concept by name alone.
Can it be trusted for this use?
Use-specific quality rules, freshness targets, ownership, and exceptions.
Treating a green technical run as business certification.

blocks.text: S3 inventory versus dataset inventory

An S3 object is a storage item; a dataset is an agreed logical unit. One dataset may span thousands of objects or multiple formats. One prefix may contain unrelated datasets, old versions, control files, and documents. If your department represents unstructured content using separate or pseudo datasets, define that mapping explicitly. Databricks cannot infer your registry boundary with certainty from a prefix.

Build a mapping with source system, bucket, canonical prefix, dataset identifier, format family, schema signature, inventory date, observed object count, coverage method, and steward. Use approved S3 inventory exports for a large estate instead of repeatedly listing buckets interactively. An inventory manifest tells you about objects; it does not read and semantically classify every value inside them.
Metadata visibility is part of the measurement

Unity Catalog information_schema provides SQL metadata and filters it by your privileges. The system form spans Unity Catalog catalogs but excludes hive_metastore metadata. Therefore, a missing row can mean absent, inaccessible, outside the selected scope, or not yet represented. Label any inventory report with principal, catalogs, filters, observation time, and known exclusions.
Sampling: useful, but not a guarantee

For an ideal independent random sample, the probability of missing a condition with prevalence p in n rows is (1-p)^n. If 1% of rows contain a rare defect, a 100-row sample still has about a 36.6% chance of missing it. Real file samples may be clustered or biased, which weakens that inference. Report the sample design and do targeted full scans when the consequence of missing a condition justifies them.

blocks.title: Why this matters to your role
blocks.text: You are building evidence that can survive a question from an application team: What did you scan, when did you scan it, which rules did you apply, and what did you not observe? A count without that context is easy to overinterpret.

sections.title: 6. Engineering concepts that make governance checks reliable

blocks.text: Bronze, silver, and gold are responsibilities

Use bronze for faithful landed records with source identifiers and ingestion metadata; silver for standardized, validated, deduplicated data; gold for business-ready metrics and consumption models. These are design conventions, not compulsory product features or quality guarantees. A table named gold_loans can still be wrong.

rows: Grain
What exactly one row represents.
A loan, a loan event, and a monthly loan snapshot need different uniqueness tests.
Business key
The identifier for the entity at the chosen grain.
A repeated loan_id is expected in an event table but may be wrong in a current-state table.
Deterministic deduplication
A documented rule always chooses the same winner.
Use event time plus a stable tie-breaker; arbitrary dropDuplicates can keep the wrong version.
Idempotency
A rerun has the intended effect without duplicate business results.
Retry-safe ingestion is different from retry-safe notifications or outbound API calls.
Event time vs ingestion time
When the business event happened versus when you received it.
A file arriving today can contain old facts. Measure the right freshness clock.
Schema enforcement vs evolution
Reject incompatible shape versus deliberately accepting changes.
Automatic acceptance of a new field is not automatic glossary mapping or release approval.
CDC vs file ingestion
CDC describes row-level changes; file ingestion discovers files.
A newly arrived snapshot is not automatically a stream of inserts, updates, and deletes.
Checkpoint
Saved streaming progress/state.
Deleting it is a reset, not a harmless cleanup; it can cause replay and duplication.

blocks.text: Spark without the jargon overload

A Spark DataFrame describes a table-like computation. Many transformations build a plan; actions such as count or a write execute it. Work is split into partitions. A join or aggregation may shuffle data between workers. One very large key can create skew, where one task takes much longer than the rest. Pulling all rows to Python with collect() or toPandas() can overwhelm the driver.

Prefer built-in SQL/DataFrame functions for ordinary cleaning. They are easier to inspect and optimize than custom Python UDFs. Use EXPLAIN and the query profile to understand scans and joins. For these tiny labs, focus on correctness; performance advice from twelve rows does not transfer to terabytes.
Delta history and changing data

A table write creates a version. History records operations, and time travel can read retained versions. It is not a permanent archive: data-file and log retention both matter, and VACUUM can remove files required by older versions. Capture the source version with your evidence, and follow a separate retention plan if an audit must be reproducible months later.

rows: Ad hoc SQL profile
Counts, nulls, ranges, uniqueness, and unusual values during investigation.
That tomorrow will look the same or that a sampled scan covers all records.

Explicit tests such as balance >= 0, required owner, or valid domain.
Correctness of the rule itself; the steward must approve its meaning.

Check records during supported declarative pipeline processing; retain metrics, drop rows, or fail updates.
Every cross-table business control. Expectations have expression restrictions.

Trend column statistics, slices, and distribution drift over time.
That an unusual value is erroneous or a stable value is correct.
Anomaly detection
Identify freshness/completeness changes against historical patterns.
A complete business-rule suite or proof that every low-priority table was scanned.

blocks.text: Current data profiling offers snapshot, time-series, and inference analysis. It requires Unity Catalog, SQL access, and documented table-management privileges; its computation uses serverless jobs infrastructure. A snapshot refresh scans the table, so estimate cost before enabling recurring profiles broadly. If unavailable, store the SQL metrics from this guide in a dated results table.
Define a metric before building a chart

items: Choose the population: all raw events, latest records per loan, all catalog assets in a scope, or a sampled set.
Choose the rule and null behavior. In SQL, unknown is not true. Write IS NULL checks explicitly.
Choose the denominator. Required fields only? Active datasets only? Distinct loans only?
Choose severity and action: observe, quarantine, stop publication, or permit a documented exception.
Store evidence: rule ID/version, numerator, denominator, source version, timestamp, scope, run ID, and owner.
Separate a policy exception from a valid record. An accepted exception should remain visible in reporting.

blocks.title: Three different percentages
blocks.text: If 4 of 10 latest loans have hard-rule violations, the affected-record rate is 40%. If one record fails two rules, the count of failed checks can exceed four. A combined average of rule pass rates is a different metric. Never label all three simply quality score.

sections.title: 8. Access, classification, lineage, and audit evidence

blocks.text: Privileges answer what an identity may do

Reading a table normally needs the relevant catalog/schema usage permissions and SELECT on the object. Creating a managed table needs CREATE TABLE in the target schema. Ownership and management privileges allow broader changes. A job may run as a service principal rather than you, so your interactive success does not establish that the scheduled run can read the same data.

Use account groups for durable access patterns when your platform team supports them. BROWSE is for discovering metadata; it does not grant SELECT. Inspect both inherited and object-level grants. Revoking a direct grant does not remove a separate inherited grant. Unity Catalog grants do not replace cloud IAM, workspace ACLs, or source database permissions.
Classification is a claim; protection is enforcement

A tag that says sensitive does not, by itself, hide values. A row filter limits visible records, a column mask changes visible values, and ABAC policies can apply controls according to governed tags. Automatic classification can suggest or assign sensitivity categories, but your data types, supported coverage, and false positives/negatives still need validation. Treat changes to security-relevant tags as controlled changes.

Table-level masks are convenient for a focused exercise. Central policies can be better for consistent coverage across many tables. ABAC support, compute requirements, and limitations evolve; the current documentation also labels certain newer policy types Beta. Ask the platform owner which mechanisms are approved instead of enabling a preview just to match a tutorial.
Lineage is observed dependency evidence

Use captured table and column dependencies to investigate a report and assess release impact. Prefer named Unity Catalog tables rather than direct file paths for column-lineage capture. External steps need supported external-lineage registration or another lineage integration. Absence of a visible edge is not proof of no dependency: permissions, unsupported execution paths, and renames can affect the graph.

The current lineage documentation distinguishes UI history from system-table retention: Catalog Explorer retains captured history from September 2024 onward, while lineage system tables expose a rolling year. Neither is a substitute for an intentionally retained release evidence package.
Audit is a different question from lineage

Lineage asks what depends on what. Audit records describe events and identities. Query history explains execution. Table history explains data-changing operations. A release review may need all four. Limit access to audit/query text and profile results because evidence itself can contain sensitive metadata or values.

blocks.text: Serverless means you manage less infrastructure, not that computation is free. Your bill can involve Databricks usage, applicable cloud infrastructure, storage, requests, data movement, and additional services. Contract rates differ from public list prices. Use the company platform team for an actual budget; do not infer a dollar estimate from a warehouse size alone.
Your first cost habits

items: Keep the initial labs tiny and run them manually. Pause your own schedules when finished.
Select only needed columns and restrict relevant dates/partitions. LIMIT alone is not a general scan-cost guarantee.
For catalog inventory, filter catalogs and schemas; information_schema LIMIT does not provide pushdown savings.
Persist useful aggregate metrics when repeated full-table scans are wasteful. Record when those metrics were calculated.

Understand OPTIMIZE, liquid clustering, and predictive optimization before adding manual maintenance jobs. More maintenance is not always better.

List-price estimates require time-effective prices and should be labeled estimates; private discounts and cloud charges can make them differ from the invoice. sections.title: Lab 2. Create the synthetic loan event dataset
sections.intro: 25-40 minutes • Lab 1; CREATE TABLE in your schema

blocks.text: Goal: create a reproducible dataset with deliberate defects. Each row is a loan event, not a unique loan. Every email is fictional and uses the reserved example.test domain. The data is deliberately too small for performance conclusions.

blocks.title: Reset behavior
blocks.text: CREATE OR REPLACE resets this lab table. Run this setup before the exercises, not inside the recurring job you build later. Existing downstream objects are not automatically recalculated by resetting bronze.

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE bronze_loans USING DELTA AS
SELECT event_id, loan_id, balance_raw, state, status, email,
       CAST(concat('2026-10-01 ', event_time) AS TIMESTAMP)
         AS event_ts,
       'synthetic_seed_v1' AS source_batch
FROM VALUES
 (1, 'L1001','250000','VA','Current','a@example.test','10:00'),
 (2, 'L1002','180000','FL','Current','b@example.test','10:00'),
 (3, 'L1003','-500',  'NJ','Current','c@example.test','10:00'),
 (4, 'L1004','125000','ZZ','Current','d@example.test','10:00'),
 (5, 'L1005','300000','VA','Unknown','e@example.test','10:00'),
 (6, 'L1006','150000','FL','Current',NULL,            '10:00'),
 (7, 'L1007',NULL,    'VA','Current','g@example.test','10:00'),
 (8, 'L1008','95000', 'NJ','Paid',   'h@example.test','10:00'),
 (9, 'L1002','179000','FL','Current','b@example.test','11:00'),
 (10,'L1008','0',     'NJ','Paid',   'h@example.test','11:00'),
 (11,'L1009','210000','VA','Delinquent','bad-email',  '10:00'),
 (12,'L1010','500000','VA','Current','j@example.test','10:00')
AS v(event_id,loan_id,balance_raw,state,status,email,event_time);

SELECT COUNT(*) AS events,
       COUNT(DISTINCT loan_id) AS distinct_loans
FROM bronze_loans;
Expected: 12 events and 10 distinct loans. L1002 and L1008 each have two events. The newer L1008 event has a zero balance and Paid status; that is a valid latest state under the exercise rules.

Only VA, FL, and NJ are valid in this fictional portfolio. Do not reuse this small reference table as a real list of U.S. states. balance_raw is intentionally a string, as it might be in a file landing area.
Evidence to keep
Save the setup query as 00_setup_synthetic_loans. Capture the 12/10 counts and the table name. In Catalog Explorer, find the same table and compare its columns with DESCRIBE TABLE.

sections.title: Lab 3. Build a metadata inventory

blocks.text: Goal: produce a small, defensible catalog report without scanning business values. Query metadata first, then enrich a table and field with descriptions.

SELECT table_catalog, table_schema, table_name,
       table_type, table_owner, comment
FROM system.information_schema.tables
WHERE table_catalog = current_catalog()
  AND table_schema = 'dg_sam_lab'
ORDER BY table_name;

SELECT table_name, ordinal_position, column_name,
       data_type, is_nullable, comment
FROM system.information_schema.columns
WHERE table_catalog = current_catalog()
  AND table_schema = 'dg_sam_lab'
ORDER BY table_name, ordinal_position;

If your schema name differs, replace the literal filter too. Expected immediately after Lab 2: bronze_loans and state_ref appear, with 8 and 2 columns respectively. Later labs add more objects, so the table count will increase.

items: Rerun the metadata query and confirm the description.
In Catalog Explorer, compare SQL object owner with the person you would call business steward. Write why they can differ.
Save the queries as inventory_tables and inventory_columns. Add your principal, catalog/schema filters, and observation time to any exported result.
Optional: if APPLY TAG and the relevant tag policy allow it, add an agreed lab-only classification tag in Catalog Explorer. Do not add a production security tag for experimentation.

blocks.text: Expected reasoning

Metadata inventory is cheap relative to full profiling and can reveal missing descriptions, unexpected types, and unowned business responsibilities. An empty comment does not prove that the company lacks a definition; it may be documented in Collibra and not synchronized here.

sections.title: Lab 4. Profile the data and explain the defects

blocks.text: Goal: distinguish raw-event observations from a latest-loan quality score. Start with an explicit scan of the 12 synthetic events.

SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS events,
  COUNT(DISTINCT loan_id) AS loans,
  SUM(CASE WHEN balance_raw IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
    AS missing_balance,
  SUM(CASE WHEN try_cast(balance_raw AS DECIMAL(18,2)) < 0
           THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS negative_balance,
  SUM(CASE WHEN email IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
    AS missing_email,
  SUM(CASE WHEN email IS NOT NULL AND email NOT LIKE '%@%.%'
           THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS malformed_email
FROM bronze_loans;

SELECT loan_id, COUNT(*) AS events
FROM bronze_loans
GROUP BY loan_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

sections.title: Lab 5. Build silver data, a quarantine, and gold metrics
sections.intro: 60-90 minutes • Labs 2 and 4; CREATE TABLE and views

blocks.text: Goal: implement a transparent quality policy. First select the latest event per loan, then evaluate hard errors. This order prevents silently reviving an older good row when the newest state is bad. Email issues are warnings in this example and do not block inclusion.

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver_loan_review USING DELTA AS
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
    PARTITION BY loan_id
    ORDER BY event_ts DESC, event_id DESC
  ) AS rn
  FROM bronze_loans
), latest AS (
  SELECT event_id, loan_id,
         try_cast(balance_raw AS DECIMAL(18,2)) AS balance,
         state, status, email, event_ts, source_batch
  FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1
)
SELECT l.*,
  concat_ws(';',
    CASE WHEN l.balance IS NULL THEN 'balance_missing_or_invalid' END,
    CASE WHEN l.balance < 0 THEN 'balance_negative' END,
    CASE WHEN s.state_code IS NULL THEN 'state_invalid' END,
    CASE WHEN l.status IS NULL OR
                   l.status NOT IN ('Current','Delinquent','Paid')
         THEN 'status_invalid' END
  ) AS hard_errors,
  CASE WHEN l.email IS NULL THEN 'email_missing'
       WHEN l.email NOT LIKE '%@%.%' THEN 'email_format'
       ELSE '' END AS warnings
FROM latest l
LEFT JOIN state_ref s ON l.state = s.state_code;

blocks.text: Why quarantine rather than erase

The quarantine preserves the latest invalid record, a reason, and a source reference. It enables remediation and reconciliation. Dropping invalid records without reporting them makes a downstream portfolio look artificially complete. Your dashboard should disclose that four latest loans were excluded from the valid-balance metric.

sections.title: Lab 7. Make updates reproducible with MERGE and history
sections.intro: 40-60 minutes • Lab 5; MODIFY on your lab copy

blocks.text: Goal: distinguish business idempotency from table operation history. Work on a separate copy so the baseline scorecard remains unchanged.

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE loan_current_demo USING DELTA AS
SELECT loan_id, balance, state, status, event_ts
FROM silver_loans_valid;

CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP VIEW loan_update AS
SELECT 'L1001' AS loan_id,
       CAST(249000 AS DECIMAL(18,2)) AS balance,
       'VA' AS state, 'Current' AS status,
       TIMESTAMP '2026-10-02 10:00:00' AS event_ts;

MERGE INTO loan_current_demo t
USING loan_update s ON t.loan_id = s.loan_id
WHEN MATCHED AND s.event_ts > t.event_ts THEN UPDATE SET
  t.balance=s.balance, t.state=s.state,
  t.status=s.status, t.event_ts=s.event_ts
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT
  (loan_id,balance,state,status,event_ts)
VALUES (s.loan_id,s.balance,s.state,s.status,s.event_ts);

SELECT COUNT(*) AS loans, SUM(balance) AS balance
FROM loan_current_demo;
DESCRIBE HISTORY loan_current_demo;

sections.intro: 60-90 minutes • Optional: Lab 8 and supported streaming notebook compute

blocks.text: Goal: observe the difference between discovering files, parsing nested content, and building a business dataset. Use an explicit schema, a persistent checkpoint, and a finite availableNow trigger. Keep the same paths for reruns.

import json
CATALOG = "your_catalog"
SCHEMA = "dg_sam_lab"
base = f"/Volumes/{CATALOG}/{SCHEMA}/lab_files"
inbox = f"{base}/json_inbox"
checkpoint = f"{base}/checkpoints/loan_json_v1"
target = f"{CATALOG}.{SCHEMA}.json_loan_events"
dbutils.fs.mkdirs(inbox)
record = {"loan_id":"J3001", "balance":125000.0,
          "borrower":{"state":"VA"},
          "flags":["new","review"]}
dbutils.fs.put(f"{inbox}/batch_001.json",
               json.dumps(record) + "\n", overwrite=False)

schema = """loan_id STRING, balance DOUBLE,
borrower STRUCT<state:STRING>, flags ARRAY<STRING>"""
incoming = (spark.readStream.format("cloudFiles")
    .option("cloudFiles.format", "json")
    .schema(schema)
    .load(inbox))

query = (incoming.writeStream
    .option("checkpointLocation", checkpoint)
    .trigger(availableNow=True)
    .toTable(target))
query.awaitTermination()
display(spark.table(target))

Expected first run: one row. Rerun only the ingestion block, without recreating or overwriting the source file: still one row. Add batch_002.json with J3002 and rerun: two rows. If you reset the checkpoint or target independently, these expectations no longer apply.

For the first record, explode produces two rows because there are two flags. This changes the grain. Summing balance after that explosion would double-count the first loan unless you account for the new grain.
Stretch: intentional schema drift

Write a third file with a new field, interest_rate. Observe whether it is ignored or rescued under your configured options; do not assume it automatically becomes a typed column with an explicit schema. Document how you would detect, review, and deliberately promote the new field. Consult schema-evolution options before changing the pipeline.
If it fails

Check READ/WRITE VOLUME, CREATE TABLE, supported compute, source syntax, and checkpoint permissions. A restricted serverless environment may reject an unsupported option or API. Use the vendor-supported finite trigger and do not delete checkpoint state as the first troubleshooting step.

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW dq_scorecard AS
SELECT COUNT(*) AS latest_loans,
  SUM(CASE WHEN hard_errors <> '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
    AS quarantined_loans,
  SUM(CASE WHEN warnings <> '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
    AS loans_with_warnings,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN hard_errors = '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
        / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0), 2) AS hard_rule_pass_pct
FROM silver_loan_review;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW dq_rule_breakdown AS
SELECT 'balance_missing_or_invalid' AS rule_id, COUNT(*) AS failures
FROM silver_loan_review WHERE balance IS NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT 'balance_negative', COUNT(*)
FROM silver_loan_review WHERE balance < 0
UNION ALL
SELECT 'state_invalid', COUNT(*)
FROM silver_loan_review WHERE state IS NULL OR state NOT IN ('VA','FL','NJ')
UNION ALL
SELECT 'status_invalid', COUNT(*)
FROM silver_loan_review
WHERE status IS NULL OR status NOT IN ('Current','Delinquent','Paid');

The assertions verify this fixed teaching fixture and detect accidental logic changes. They are not suitable production thresholds. A real job validates contracts such as key uniqueness, plausible volume changes, approved rule behavior, and source reconciliation. A known quarantine population may be an expected outcome rather than a job failure.
Retries need a purpose

Retry transient service or network failures. Repeatedly retrying an invalid schema or a deterministic assertion does not fix it. If a workflow creates an issue, sends an email, or updates Collibra, use a durable idempotency key such as dataset ID + observation/run ID + action type so a retry does not duplicate the side effect.

  CONSTRAINT balance_parseable EXPECT (balance IS NOT NULL),
  CONSTRAINT balance_nonnegative EXPECT (balance >= 0)
)
AS SELECT event_id, loan_id,
          try_cast(balance_raw AS DECIMAL(18,2)) AS balance
FROM your_catalog.dg_sam_lab.bronze_loans;

blocks.text: A. Store a run-level scorecard

Run after the baseline lab. This illustrates a results model; a production run should supply stable run and source-version identifiers from orchestration. The MERGE protects the same run key from duplicate insertion. Use a new run key for a new observation, and never overwrite an audit record casually.

Expected baseline: one record for lab_baseline_001 with 10 latest loans, 4 quarantined, 2 warnings, and 60.00% pass. Rerunning with the same key preserves the first observation. Add source table version, source scope, principal, compute/run link, and per-rule details to make this suitable as actual evidence.
B. Report missing column descriptions

SELECT table_name, column_name, data_type
FROM system.information_schema.columns
WHERE table_catalog = current_catalog()
  AND table_schema = 'dg_sam_lab'
  AND (comment IS NULL OR trim(comment) = '')
ORDER BY table_name, ordinal_position;
This is a metadata-completeness queue, not proof of missing business definitions. Join to your approved mapping and documentation sources before opening remediation items.
C. Snapshot a schema and review change

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS column_baseline USING DELTA AS
SELECT table_catalog, table_schema, table_name, column_name,
       data_type, is_nullable
FROM system.information_schema.columns
WHERE table_catalog = current_catalog()
  AND table_schema = 'dg_sam_lab'
  AND table_name = 'bronze_loans';

WITH now_cols AS (
  SELECT table_catalog, table_schema, table_name, column_name,
         data_type, is_nullable
  FROM system.information_schema.columns
  WHERE table_catalog = current_catalog()
    AND table_schema = 'dg_sam_lab'
    AND table_name = 'bronze_loans'
)
SELECT coalesce(b.column_name,n.column_name) AS column_name,
       b.data_type AS before_type, n.data_type AS after_type,
       CASE WHEN b.column_name IS NULL THEN 'added'
            WHEN n.column_name IS NULL THEN 'missing_or_not_visible'
            ELSE 'definition_changed' END AS change
FROM column_baseline b
FULL OUTER JOIN now_cols n
  ON b.table_catalog=n.table_catalog
 AND b.table_schema=n.table_schema
 AND b.table_name=n.table_name
 AND b.column_name=n.column_name
WHERE b.column_name IS NULL OR n.column_name IS NULL
   OR b.data_type <> n.data_type OR b.is_nullable <> n.is_nullable;

Expected initially: zero changes. This simplified comparison does not infer renames or compare comments, nested schemas, masks, tags, or constraints. A production snapshot must record its scope and identity so lost visibility is not mistaken for a deleted field.
D. Separate freshness clocks

SELECT MAX(event_ts) AS latest_business_event,
       current_timestamp() AS checked_at,
       timestampdiff(HOUR, MAX(event_ts), current_timestamp())
         AS hours_since_latest_event
FROM bronze_loans;

The historical synthetic data will naturally look old. This query teaches a clock, not a production SLA. For real data add received_at and pipeline_completed_at, then define separate source-delivery and processing targets. Use UTC consistently and document the business timezone.
E. Inspect permitted usage without inventing a dollar bill

-- Optional: administrator-granted billing-system-table access.
SELECT usage_date, workspace_id, sku_name, usage_unit,
       SUM(usage_quantity) AS usage_quantity
FROM system.billing.usage
WHERE usage_date >= date_sub(current_date(), 7)
GROUP BY usage_date, workspace_id, sku_name, usage_unit
ORDER BY usage_date DESC, workspace_id, sku_name;

Use your authorized workspace filter before distributing results. Keep corrections/retractions in the usage accounting rather than retaining only original records. If you add pricing, match SKU, cloud, unit, currency, and effective time; check for missing or multiple price matches. Treat the result as a list-price estimate, not the contracted invoice.

sections.title: 12. P2P releases: evidence, promotion, and recovery

blocks.text: A release has at least three separate pieces: versioned code/resources, data and metadata changes, and the governance decision. A successful deployment command proves only one piece. Keep your existing approval workflow and use Databricks evidence to make that decision better informed.

headers: What you do as a practitioner
rows: Develop
Implement in a personal/dev scope; use synthetic or approved data; define grain, rules, and expected behavior.
Steward for meaning; platform owner for permitted access.
Review
Submit code/configuration changes, test evidence, impacted objects, and open issues.
Peer reviewer and affected data owners.
Test
Deploy the same version with test configuration; test identities, bad inputs, reruns, and failures.
Release/test owners; source teams as needed.
Approve
Present complete evidence and any exceptions.
Your established approvers, not an automatically generated dashboard.
Promote
Deploy approved code/configuration under the designated identity.
Authorized delivery owner or automation.
Verify
Check the first production run, outputs, metadata sync, lineage observations, and notifications.
Operational owner and consumers.
Recover
Use the approved rollback/rebuild procedure and reconcile any downstream effects.
Platform/delivery owners and affected teams.

blocks.text: Why bundles matter

Declarative Automation Bundles put resource definitions and code under version control with environment-specific configuration. Learn to separate a transformation from deployment details such as catalog, schema, compute policy, and run-as identity. Do not copy a production workspace URL or privileged principal into a learning template.

# Conceptual bundle fragment; not a complete deployment project.
bundle:
  name: governance_quality_pilot
variables:
  catalog:
    description: Approved target catalog
  schema:
    description: Approved target schema
targets:
  dev:
    mode: development
    variables:
      catalog: your_dev_catalog
      schema: dg_sam_lab
  test:
    variables:
      catalog: your_test_catalog
      schema: governance_test

To practice, create an approved Git folder, commit the lab code, use a vendor-approved bundle starter, add a job resource, run bundle validation, and deploy only to the assigned dev target. Inspect the generated job before running it. The fragment above deliberately omits authentication and resource definitions; use the current bundle tutorial for a complete project.
Release gates worth proposing

items: Schema and grain are documented; breaking changes have consumer review.
Required mappings are approved or have named exceptions.
Quality results reconcile to the source population and retain rejected records/evidence.
Effective access and dashboard sharing are tested using the intended identities.
Retries and reprocessing are safe; transient and data-contract failures are handled differently.
Code version, configuration, job run, and source data version are traceable.
Retention supports the promised rollback; outbound catalog changes can be reconciled.

sections.title: 13. Use AI features as assisted work with review

blocks.text: The most useful AI starting point for you is help drafting SQL, explaining a query plan, or suggesting metadata descriptions. Provide approved context and ask for reasoning, then verify against a known result. Do not substitute an AI-generated label for a steward-approved business definition.
Genie and governed business questions

Current documentation describes Genie One as a business-facing experience, Genie Agents as domain-specific configured contexts, and Genie Code as the technical assistant. Older material and your sandbox may use earlier names. Configure trusted data, definitions, joins, and example questions before expecting reliable answers. Exact capabilities and charging depend on the current product and your account configuration.

rows: Write SQL for missing balances by source batch.
Compare against the explicit Lab 4 result and test null behavior.
Explain why the portfolio has six loans.
Require the raw-to-latest-to-quarantine reconciliation.
Suggest a definition for balance.
Require steward confirmation of principal vs payoff, currency, and as-of time.
Which reports could a column change affect?
Compare captured lineage with external dependencies and consumer review.
Summarize quality trends.
Check time windows, denominators, missing runs, and whether the source changed.

blocks.text: The wider AI/ML surface

MLflow and model lifecycle tools support tracking and evaluation of models and AI applications. Model serving exposes inference services; AI Search supports retrieval use cases. Databricks Apps can provide a custom interface, while Lakebase Postgres supports transactional app needs. These expand the assets your governance program may need to inventory: models, prompts, endpoints, retrieval indexes, evaluation data, and application permissions.

For a future glossary assistant, start with approved terms and evidence links. Test ambiguous questions, conflicting definitions, missing context, and unauthorized data requests. A fluent answer is not a lineage record, an access approval, or a reliable statement of policy. Review the generated SQL and its execution identity before trusting a returned number.

sections.title: 14. Capabilities and limitations: the reality check

rows: All S3 and databases are automatically inventoried.
Registration, source connections, mapping rules, and access scope are required.
Reconcile against an authoritative inventory and disclose gaps.
Unity Catalog replaces Collibra by default.
There is overlap, but your workflows, metamodel, connector behavior, and ownership determine the operating model.
Assign authority property by property.
A column tag protects data.
A tag can drive a policy; the policy and supported access path enforce protection.
Test effective access, not tag presence alone.
Lineage is complete and permanent everywhere.
Capture coverage, visibility, renames, external steps, and retention differ.
Record observed versus inferred relationships.
A primary key declaration rejects duplicates.
Current Delta primary/foreign/unique constraints are informational; NOT NULL and CHECK are enforced.
Test uniqueness and referential integrity explicitly.
Any successful job means data is good.
A job can succeed while producing wrong, empty, stale, or incomplete data.
Add meaningful assertions and reconciliation.
A quality monitor replaces business rules.
Statistical trends and freshness signals answer different questions.
Combine monitoring with approved rules and review.
Serverless supports all classic-cluster code.
Libraries, APIs, networking, configuration, and compute restrictions can differ.
Use supported examples and verify the access mode/runtime.
Federation is a free ingestion substitute.
It can use both remote and Databricks compute and is read-only in the documented federation patterns.
Consider source load, latency, repeat scans, and connector suitability.
Time travel is my backup.
Retained log and data files are required; maintenance can remove older files.
Agree retention and independent recovery requirements.
A file retry guarantees no duplicate business data.
File progress tracking does not recognize every duplicate record across files.
Use business keys and deterministic merge/dedup rules.
The dashboard honors each viewer automatically.
Shared/publisher versus individual data-permission modes differ.
Choose deliberately and test the intended audience.
The public product catalog equals my entitlement.
Cloud, region, tier, rollout, preview status, workspace policies, and grants matter.
Maintain an availability register with the vendor.
More compute fixes every slow query.
Bad joins, skew, full scans, tiny files, and repeated work can dominate.
Inspect evidence, change one variable, and remeasure.
A model can certify compliance.
Compliance decisions depend on applicable policy and approved evidence.
Keep human accountability and recorded exceptions.

blocks.text: Specific constraints to revisit as you advance

Read current feature requirements before adopting row/column policies, external clients, streaming state, table-format interoperability, or preview AI capabilities. Protocol upgrades can affect external readers/writers. Managed and external tables differ in lifecycle: dropping an external registration leaves its files, while managed objects have platform-managed recovery/deletion behavior. Do not test deletion on real data to learn that difference.

For unstructured documents, storage and retrieval are separate from extracting accurate fields. OCR or AI extraction can be wrong; validate on representative documents, retain provenance, and measure errors before using extracted data in governance decisions. A successful binary-file ingest proves that bytes arrived, not that their meaning was understood.

sections.title: 15. Troubleshooting without guessing

rows: Table not found
Current catalog/schema; exact full name; visibility; whether the task ran in a new session.
Creating a new similarly named table before resolving the original.
Permission denied
Running identity; USE permissions; object grants; inherited policy; compute/workspace access.
Requesting administrator access as the first fix.
Python works, SQL query fails
Different compute, dialect, context, or permissions; notebook-only objects.
Assuming every command works in every editor.
A temp view disappears
Session scope or different job task; persist an appropriate intermediate table if needed.
Relying on interactive state for a scheduled job.
Column cannot be cast
Unexpected strings, nulls, whitespace, formats; compare cast with try_cast.
Replacing every invalid value with zero.
MERGE fails or duplicates appear
Multiple source matches, wrong business key, target duplicates, or reset progress state.
Adding DISTINCT without defining which event wins.
No lineage shown
Registered names, supported execution, permissions, timing, and known capture limitations.
Treating an absent graph as proof of no downstream use.
Unexpectedly low quality rate
Denominator, latest-versus-raw grain, null behavior, rule version, and scope filters.
Adjusting the threshold until the tile turns green.
Job succeeds but report is stale
Refresh timing, upstream task dependency, table/view persistence, warehouse/cache behavior.
Assuming a successful downstream refresh means fresh source data.
Job fails only when scheduled
Run-as identity, libraries, parameters, environment configuration, and state assumptions.
Granting all privileges to the job principal.
Query is slow
Plan/profile, scan volume, skew, shuffle/spill, join cardinality, startup versus execution time.
Scaling first without recording a baseline.
Counts differ from Collibra
Different refresh times, identities, exclusions, object mappings, deleted/renamed assets, connector settings.
Deleting the unmatched catalog assets immediately.

blocks.text: The six-line incident note

items: Expected behavior and the business consequence.
Actual error/result with the job/query/run identifier.
Identity, compute, catalog/schema, and code version.
Inputs and source version/observation time.
Smallest reproduction and what changed since the last good run.
Next owner/action, evidence location, and current workaround.

blocks.text: This format makes you more useful to vendor and platform teams than a screenshot that says it does not work. Exclude secrets and unnecessary sensitive values from incident notes.

sections.title: 16. A department pilot you can propose as an end user

blocks.text: Propose one measurable improvement within an existing process: a repeatable metadata and quality evidence pack for one approved dataset. Your role is to demonstrate usefulness and document requirements. Platform setup, policy approval, and production operations stay with their designated owners.

rows: Days 1-10
Finish the core synthetic labs; record sandbox availability; identify one real pilot candidate with the team.
Working SQL, 12/10/6/4 reconciliation, dashboard, and a list of specific access gaps.
Days 11-20
Agree the dataset boundary, grain, business mappings, approved data access, and 3-5 meaningful rules.
Signed-off definitions or explicit unresolved questions; no invented thresholds.
Days 21-30
Run the checks on an approved sample/scope and reconcile inventory to the current catalog process.
Repeatable results, known coverage limits, measured manual effort, and named remediation owners.
Days 31-60
Schedule under an approved identity; retain results; test connector behavior on the pilot scope.
Failure/retry tests, metadata reconciliation, measured refresh reliability, and cost visibility.
Days 61-90
Prepare controlled promotion and a handoff; evaluate whether to expand.
Peer-reviewed code, release evidence, operational owner, and before/after measures.

blocks.text: Measure value without promising a number in advance

Baseline the time needed to assemble an evidence pack, the fraction of assets with verified mappings, the time between a failed rule and an assigned owner, and the rate of successful scheduled evidence runs. Compare the pilot with that baseline. Do not promise percentage savings until you observe them.
High-value questions for the vendor

items: Which cloud, region, tier, runtimes, access modes, and serverless features are enabled in this exact workspace?
What is the approved catalog/schema structure, and which privileges are appropriate for a governance practitioner?
How are S3 locations and database sources registered, and what inventory remains outside Unity Catalog?
Which Collibra connector, Edge version, lineage capability, JDBC profiling setup, and outbound mappings will be used?
Which system tables may we query, and how are operational records retained for release evidence?
Which quality-monitoring features are enabled, what do they cost, and who owns their schedules?
How are production jobs deployed, what is their run-as identity, and where does our existing release approval fit?
What happens when the vendor sandbox expires, and how do we preserve code and evidence?

sections.title: 17. Certification: target Associate, then deepen through projects

blocks.text: Start with Databricks Certified Data Engineer Associate. It fits your goal of becoming capable of building and operating data workflows, while your governance background gives you a useful advantage on controls and meaning. Governance alone will not cover the engineering portion: practice ingestion, transformations, job operations, and deployment until you can troubleshoot them.

The official page checked on 10 October 2026 links to the guide for the exam version effective 4 May 2026. It lists 45 scored multiple-choice items, 90 minutes, a USD 200 registration fee before applicable taxes, no mandatory prerequisite, and two-year validity. The guide recommends training and six months of hands-on experience. Recheck the official page and applicable guide before booking.

Chapters 1, 3, 4, and 9; choose compute and explain storage/catalog separation.
Ingestion and loading
Labs 8-9; compare COPY INTO, Auto Loader, managed connectors, and federation.
Transformations and modeling
Labs 4-7; joins, grain, null handling, deduplication, aggregation, and nested data.
Lakeflow Jobs
Lab 13; dependencies, retries, triggers, identity, monitoring, and repair.
CI/CD

blocks.text: Where this guide needs additional practice

The labs deliberately favor SQL and your governance use case. For exam readiness, also implement the transformations in PySpark, practice a managed Lakeflow Connect source with the vendor, build a complete bundle from the current starter, and inspect real query/Spark execution profiles. Work with joins and unions, arrays/structs, schema evolution, incremental processing, and the differences among views, materialized views, tables, and streaming tables.
How to use official training efficiently

Use Databricks Academy and the training linked from the current exam guide. After each topic, reproduce one example from a blank notebook, then change an assumption and explain the result. Keep an error log organized by misunderstood concept. Use official sample questions for format familiarity; avoid memorizing answers or relying on unauthorized exam dumps.
Readiness signals, not a promised pass date

items: You can rebuild the capstone without copying whole sections and explain every transformation.
You can diagnose at least five intentionally introduced errors, including permissions, null logic, duplicate keys, stale data, and bad job configuration.
You can choose between ingestion methods and compute types for a new scenario.
You can explain what a retry changes, what time travel retains, and why a tag is not a mask.
You can deploy and validate a complete dev bundle in an approved environment, then explain how test/prod differ.
You can answer unfamiliar practice scenarios by reasoning, not by matching phrases to screenshots.

blocks.text: After Associate, consider Data Engineer Professional when you have deeper experience with production pipelines, performance, observability, recovery, and delivery. Certification is a milestone. Being the person who can explain why a quality metric changed and safely fix the pipeline is the stronger evidence of expertise.

blocks.text: A weekly rhythm that reduces friction

Use two 45-minute learning sessions, two 60-minute build sessions, and one 90-minute review/rebuild session. Begin each session by writing one concrete goal. End with three lines: what worked, what broke, and what to try next. Longer weekend sessions can cover the capstone; short weekday sessions are enough for one query or one concept.
Your learning portfolio

sections.title: 19. Reasoning checks with answer notes

blocks.text: These are original practice prompts, not real exam questions. Try answering aloud before reading the answer note. The aim is to explain a decision, not memorize a term.

rows: You see 80 tables but the source inventory has 100. What do you conclude?
Only that the two scoped observations differ. Check access, source coverage, refresh time, registration, and matching before calling 20 tables missing.
The file sample has no sensitive values. Can you mark the dataset non-sensitive?
Not from that alone. Sampling can miss rare values, and classification also depends on context and policy.
A sensitive tag is present, but users still see the data. Why?
Tags do not automatically mask values. Check attached policies, grants, supported compute/path, and the testing identity.
Two loan events have the same key. Is that a duplicate defect?
It depends on grain. It is normal in an event table; a current-state table needs deterministic selection.
The newest row is invalid but yesterday's row was valid. Keep yesterday's?
Only under an explicit business policy. This guide retains the newest row and quarantines it rather than silently showing stale data.
The job retries after creating a Collibra issue. What must be protected?
The side effect: use a durable idempotency key and reconcile whether the issue was already created.
A dashboard viewer lacks SELECT but can see a chart. Is that impossible?
No. Shared/publisher data-permission mode may intentionally use a different identity. Review the approved audience and mode.
History lists an old version. Does that guarantee it is queryable?
No. Required data files and logs must both remain. History is not a long-term backup guarantee.
Why did a JSON explode double the sum?
The operation changed grain by producing a row per array element. Aggregate at the intended entity grain.
Why do 60% quality pass and 50% mapping approval not conflict?
They measure different populations and controls. Define both numerator and denominator.
A primary key is declared. Can you omit a uniqueness check?
Not merely because of the declaration: current Delta key constraints are informational.
Should a deterministic data-contract error be retried five times?
Usually no. Diagnose the input/rule problem; bounded retries are mainly useful for recoverable transient failures.

sections.title: 20. Your Databricks vocabulary sheet

rows: Account / workspace
The broader administrative boundary / a place to collaborate and run workloads.
Metastore
The governance metadata container holding catalogs and related objects.
Catalog / schema
Two organizational and permission levels above data objects.
Unity Catalog
Databricks governance layer for registered data and AI assets.
Catalog Explorer
The interface used to inspect registered objects and their details.
Table / view
Stored table data / a saved query definition over data.
Materialized view
Persisted query results maintained by refresh processing.
Streaming table
A table populated/maintained through incremental streaming processing.
Volume
Governed access to non-tabular files under a catalog and schema.
External location
An approved cloud-storage path tied to a credential and permissions.
Managed / external table
Platform-managed data lifecycle / registered data whose files have an external lifecycle.
Foreign catalog
A catalog exposing supported external-system metadata/data through federation.
Delta Lake
A table technology combining data files with transaction metadata.
Spark / PySpark
Distributed data-processing engine / its Python interface.
DataFrame
A table-like data structure and computation interface.
SQL warehouse
Compute intended for SQL workloads.
Serverless
Compute infrastructure managed by the platform; still subject to cost and limitations.
Photon
Databricks execution acceleration for supported operations.
Partition / shuffle / skew
A work/data division / movement between workers / uneven distribution of work.
Auto Loader
Incremental cloud-file discovery and ingestion using cloudFiles.
COPY INTO
SQL file loading with remembered file-ingestion progress.
CDC
A representation of inserts, updates, and deletes from a changing source.
Checkpoint
Persistent progress/state used for restartable stream processing.
Lakeflow Jobs
Task orchestration, scheduling, and operational run tracking.
Expectation
A declarative pipeline data check with configured violation behavior.
Rule / profile / anomaly
Explicit business test / measured data statistics / deviation from an expected pattern.
Lineage / audit / history
Dependencies / recorded actions / changes to table versions.
ABAC
Access control driven by attributes such as governed tags.
Mask / row filter
A transformation of visible column values / restriction of visible records.
Principal / run-as
A user, group, or service identity / the identity executing a job.
Service principal
A non-human identity used by applications and automation.
Metric view
A reusable governed definition of business measures and dimensions.
Idempotent
Safe to rerun with the intended business effect occurring only once.
Bundle
Versioned configuration and code used to deploy workspace resources.
SLA / SLO
An agreed service commitment / a measurable service objective.
Quarantine
Retained invalid records with reasons and remediation context.
Data contract
An agreed interface: shape, grain, meaning, quality, ownership, and change expectations.
